summary: Speakers, addressees (u to McGonagall, jullie to both parents, je from McGonagall), the biting double act, the fixed motif in b053 and the zebra punchline all survive. Three reader-visible stumbles (one referent, two wrong-sense) and a few hedges flattened.

findings.problem: The previous line (b045) is Harry's, so 'hem' attaches to Harry: the mother seems to back Harry instead of seconding the father's sarcasm.
findings.evidence: EN: '“Of course,” seconded Harry’s mother.' (seconding the father, b044) vs NL: '“Natuurlijk,” viel Harry’s moeder hem bij.'
findings.required_fix: Name the father: '“Natuurlijk,” viel Harry’s moeder zijn vader bij.' (or 'Harry’s moeder sloot zich bij haar man aan').

findings.problem: 'Daar!' reads as pointing at a place ('over there'), not as the triumphant 'There!' of 'I told you so'.
findings.evidence: EN: '“There! You see what I have to deal with?”' vs NL: '“Daar! Ziet u het? Dit moet ik elke dag verdragen!”'
findings.required_fix: Use 'Ziet u wel!' (e.g. '“Ziet u wel? Dit moet ik verdragen!”'); drop the added 'elke dag' while there.

findings.fragment: Zweinstein kan de basis prima leren
findings.problem: Without an indirect object 'leren' reads as 'learn': Hogwarts itself learning the basics, not teaching them.
findings.evidence: EN: 'Hogwarts is quite capable of teaching the basics.' vs NL: 'Zweinstein kan de basis prima leren.'
findings.required_fix: Make it teaching: 'Op Zweinstein leer je de basis prima.' or 'Zweinstein kan je de basis prima leren.'

findings.fragment: Praten ging haar om de een of andere reden moeilijk.
findings.problem: The narrator's coy 'seemed to be' is dropped. 'for some reason' keeps most of the irony, so the joke still reads.
findings.evidence: EN: 'Professor McGonagall seemed to be having trouble speaking for some reason' vs NL: 'Praten ging haar om de een of andere reden moeilijk.'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Praten leek haar om de een of andere reden moeilijk te gaan.'

findings.problem: The hedge 'I can't recall hearing about' becomes a flat 'I don't know such a thing'. Her calm, cautious tone is a little flattened.
findings.evidence: EN: '“I can’t recall hearing about such a condition before…”' vs NL: '“Zoiets ken ik niet…”'
findings.required_fix: Optional: '“Ik heb nog nooit van zoiets gehoord, denk ik…”'

findings.fragment: Ik hoef niet te lijden onder ... : het levert geen leraren
findings.problem: 'on grounds that' is softened into a second statement, and 'should not have to' into 'do not have to'. The colon still carries the justification, so the over-formal joke holds.
findings.evidence: EN: 'on grounds that I should not have to suffer for ... failure to provide teachers' vs NL: 'Ik hoef niet te lijden onder het falen ...: het levert geen leraren ...'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Want ik hoor niet te lijden onder ...'

findings.fragment: Voor hen was het één grote grap.
findings.problem: 'like they thought it was all a big joke' (Harry's indignant view) becomes a narrator statement of fact. The indignation is a little weaker.
findings.evidence: EN: 'like they thought it was all a big joke' vs NL: 'Voor hen was het één grote grap.'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Alsof het één grote grap was.'

findings.problem: 'try to' is dropped: in English the attempt fails; in Dutch he actually gets up early. The point (it makes no difference) survives.
findings.evidence: EN: 'Even if I try to wake up early, it makes no difference' vs NL: 'Ook als ik vroeg opsta, maakt het geen verschil.'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Ook als ik probeer vroeg op te staan, …'
